::: {#heading}
### About Me

I am an assistant professor at the College of William & Mary, jointly appointed in the Department of [Government](https://www.wm.edu/as/government/) and the [Environment & Sustainability Program](https://www.wm.edu/as/environment/). I am interested in how economic and security concerns affect support for environmental protection. In my dissertation, I examine how international economic competition affects environmental support in the U.S. Congress and among the American public. I strive to pursue a variety of research methods, including observational studies, text analysis, and survey experiments.

Before coming to the academia, I interned at the headquarter of the U.N.E.S.C.O and KOICA as an undergraduate, and worked in the non-profit sector in South Korea for about a year after graduating college.

In my free time, I like watching movies (all genres except for horror), collecting books (maybe more so than reading them), and travelling (to explore cafés and bakeries).
